example_2: Give me a map and I'll find the coast; give me a tide chart and I'll find the coast.
example_3: If it rains, the fair goes on. If it floods, the fair goes on.

definition: Piling up a breathless heap of descriptive words, often in an insult.
example_1: That mangy, moaning, spring-sprung, coffee-stained impostor of a couch has outlived three apartments.
example_2: The storm was a howling, fence-flattening, laundry-thieving, picnic-erasing menace.
example_3: He described the old mower as a sputtering, backfiring, grass-ignoring monument to false hope.

definition: A part standing for the whole, or the whole for a part.
example_1: All hands met the ferry; every hand had a name.
example_2: The ranch ran two hundred head that winter.
example_3: Nice wheels — the whole car, judged by its rims.

definition: Describing one sense in terms of another — loud colors, sweet sounds.
example_1: Her laugh tasted like lemonade at the wrong hour.
example_2: The trumpet threw bright orange across the dim bar.
example_3: His name sounded green, like new mint.

definition: The arrangement of words into phrases and sentences — order as meaning.
example_1: 'Only she paid' and 'she only paid' fight over one adverb.
example_2: Short sentences. Then shorter. The panic shows in the syntax.
example_3: The contract's single 200-word sentence was the trap.

definition: A composition in which every word begins with the same letter.
example_1: Seven sleepy sailors silently stacked salted sardines.
example_2: Bella's bakery boasts big, buttery, braided breads.
example_3: Wandering wallabies wearily watched wilting wildflowers.

definition: Saying the same thing twice in different words, deliberately, for emphasis or comedy.
example_1: It's a free gift, at no cost, included.
example_2: The meeting is at 3 p.m. in the afternoon, he confirmed, confirming it.
example_3: We arrived at our final destination, which is where we ended up.

definition: Impressive-sounding pseudo-technical language deployed for effect.
example_1: The blender's box promised a quad-vortex torque matrix with adaptive smoothie telemetry.
example_2: I can't fix the door, but I can recalibrate its hinge-flux dampeners, said the roommate, holding one screwdriver.
example_3: The sales pitch cited proprietary cloud-synergized nano-filtration, which turned out to be a sponge.

definition: The central idea a work keeps returning to — what it is about beneath the plot.
example_1: Under the heist, the book is about what debt does to friendship.
example_2: Every subplot circles the same question: who gets to be believed?
example_3: The film's theme is inheritance — of houses, of tempers, of silence.

definition: Third-person narration confined to one character's perceptions and thoughts.
example_1: The story follows Omar through the auction, and we learn the reserve price only when he does, one paddle too late.
example_2: She watches the harbor lights and wonders what her sister decided; the narration, loyal to her, wonders too.
example_3: We know the trail only as Priya knows it: by the blazes she finds and the one, crucially, she misses.

definition: A deadline that squeezes the characters and cranks the suspense (also called a ticking time bomb scenario).
example_1: The visa expires Friday; the wedding is Saturday; the embassy closes for a holiday nobody checked.
example_2: The tide will cover the sandbar at six, and the metal detector has just started beeping.
example_3: Forty minutes to judging, and the show cake is still, structurally speaking, a suggestion.

definition: The moment a work's own title is spoken within the work.
example_1: In the last chapter of The Long Portage, the guide finally shrugs: every good route has one long portage.
example_2: The play is called Second Chair, and the whole audience inhales when the conductor finally says it aloud.
example_3: The memoir Borrowed Ladders earns its name on the final page, in the neighbor's driveway, ladder in hand.

definition: Splitting a word open and inserting another word inside it.
example_1: That performance was fan-flipping-tastic.
example_2: This is a whole nother problem.
example_3: La-dee-freaking-da, said the teenager, alphabetizing the garage as instructed.

definition: A quoted remark paired with an adverb or verb that puns on it.
example_1: I hate camping, she said intently.
example_2: The lights are out, he said darkly.
example_3: I dropped the toothpaste, said Dad, crestfallen.

definition: The author's attitude toward the subject, carried by word choice and rhythm.
example_1: The recipe's tone was pure ultimatum: fold, do not stir, or else.
example_2: She reviewed the gala with a straight face and a raised eyebrow.
example_3: The field guide describes wasps with open admiration and mild fear.

definition: A narrative in which a protagonist's flaw or fate drives them to ruin.
example_1: The union founder falsifies one signature to save the union, and loses it.
example_2: Oedipus investigates a crime that turns out to be his own biography.
example_3: She wins the seat by burying the story that would have freed her brother.

definition: A series of three parallel elements, rising to a satisfying close.
example_1: Pack the van, kiss the dog, wave until the house is small.
example_2: The recipe asks for patience, butter, and more patience.
example_3: She came home with a sunburn, a trophy, and a story that improved yearly.

definition: Deliberately representing something as smaller or milder than it is.
example_1: The bridge is out, so the detour adds a moment or two.
example_2: Losing the deed was a bit of a hiccup.
example_3: The volcano made rather a mess of the runway.

definition: A narrator whose account the reader learns to distrust.
example_1: I only borrowed the canoe, our narrator insists, in a chapter that mentions, in passing, three other borrowed canoes.
example_2: The diary swears the diet is going beautifully; the pantry inventory keeps its own diary.
example_3: According to the groundskeeper, the hedge maze has never lost a single visitor; the flyer he hands out lists an exit hotline.

definition: A repeated pet phrase or filler that characterizes a speaker.
example_1: The harbor master ends every sentence with 'as the tide allows,' including his wedding vows.
example_2: You could transcribe the coach by his tic alone: at the end of the day, at the end of the day, at the end of the day.
example_3: Her grandfather prefaced everything, even dessert, with 'now, I'm no expert.'

definition: The believable texture of truth in fiction — details that make the invented feel real.
example_1: The fake diner felt real because the ketchup bottle was half empty.
example_2: Her invented town has bus routes, feuds, and a broken clock everyone consults.
example_3: The courtroom scenes convince because the lawyers are mostly bored.

definition: Writing arranged in metrical or deliberate lines — poetry as a form, or a single line of it.
example_1: The invitation came in rhymed verse, which explained the RSVP delay.
example_2: He kept a verse from an old hymn folded in his toolbox.
example_3: Blank verse marches ten syllables at a time, unrhymed and unbothered.

definition: A brief, impressionistic scene that captures a moment rather than a plot.
example_1: One page: a bus shelter at dawn, two strangers sharing one dry square meter, neither speaking, both guarding the same bakery bag smell.
example_2: The chapter is just the grandmother's hands sorting buttons by feel while the radio hums the shipping forecast.
example_3: A half page in the laundromat: folding warm towels, watching snow decide, missing no one for exactly four minutes.

definition: The turn in a poem or argument where the direction pivots.
example_1: For eight lines the sonnet praises the tidy garden; at the ninth it admits the weeds were the only part she planted.
example_2: The toast lists every reason the couple should never have worked, then turns: and yet, here is the harbor they built.
example_3: The essay spends three paragraphs defending the shortcut, pivots on one 'but,' and spends the rest apologizing to the scenic route.

definition: A saying, a speaker, and a literal situation combined for comic effect.
example_1: 'Everything comes to a point,' said the pencil, entering the sharpener.
example_2: 'I'm feeling run down,' said the battery, dimming the flashlight.
example_3: 'We'll cross that bridge when we come to it,' said the ferry captain, steering straight past it.

definition: One word, usually a verb, governing two objects in different senses (also called syllepsis).
example_1: She held her breath and the door for the movers.
example_2: He lost the map, the trail, and finally his sense of humor about both.
example_3: The storm took the power lines and our excuses for skipping game night.

definition: Giving animal qualities to humans, objects, or abstractions.
example_1: The old tractor growled awake, shook its haunches, and prowled the field rows.
example_2: By 5 p.m. the inbox was a hive, swarming and unswattable.
example_3: The toddler wolfed his noodles, then perched on the armrest like a satisfied owl.
